title: Universal Eigenvector Statistics of Non-Hermitian Random Matrices
authors: Ze Chen, Zhenyu Xiao, Shinsei Ryu
abstract: Eigenvector overlaps quantify nonorthogonality and govern the response and dynamics of non-Hermitian systems. We extend the universality of non-Hermitian random matrices to the statistics of these overlaps. We obtain analytical expressions for eigenvector overlaps in the spectral bulk and near the origin, covering ten symmetry classes in the limit of large matrix size. Using fermionic replica nonlinear $σ$ models, we relate these overlaps to Hermitian level statistics, symmetry class by symmetry class and topological sector by topological sector. Numerical calculations in various physical models support the universality of the normalized overlaps in the regimes studied. Our work establishes a duality between Hermitian level statistics and non-Hermitian eigenvector overlaps.
summary: This work investigates the statistics of eigenvector overlaps in non-Hermitian random matrices, extending universality beyond eigenvalues. Using advanced techniques like replica sigma models, the authors derive analytical results for these overlaps across ten symmetry classes. The key finding is the establishment of a duality connecting non-Hermitian eigenvector statistics directly to known Hermitian spectral correlations.
main_problem: The paper extends the concept of universality from eigenvalue statistics to the statistics of eigenvector overlaps in non-Hermitian random matrices.
main_result: It establishes a duality between Hermitian level statistics and non-Hermitian eigenvector overlaps, providing analytical expressions for these overlaps across ten symmetry classes.
method: The analysis employs fermionic replica nonlinear sigma models to derive analytical expressions for the overlaps in the spectral bulk and near the origin.
model_or_system: The study focuses on non-Hermitian random matrices, covering ensembles characterized by ten Altland-Zirnbauer (AZ0) symmetry classes, and relates findings to physical models like the non-Hermitian Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model.
key_observables: Eigenvector overlaps (diagonal $O_1$ and off-diagonal $O_2$), eigenvalue densities, and spectral correlations.
important_parameters: The results are derived in the limit of large matrix size ($N 	o \infty$), and the universality depends on symmetry classes ($	ext{TRS}^\dagger$, $	ext{PHS}$, $	ext{SLS}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the existence of a statistical rotation symmetry for the random matrix ensemble.
figures_summary: The notes mention Tables I, II, and III summarizing the ten symmetry classes, the bulk diagonal and normalized off-diagonal overlaps for the three main families (A, $	ext{AI}^\dagger$, $	ext{AII}^\dagger$), and the hard-edge diagonal overlaps.
paper_structure: The paper structure involves reviewing the symmetries, presenting the replica calculation using the sigma model, and comparing the derived predictions with numerical results from various physical models.
why_interesting: The established duality between Hermitian and non-Hermitian spectral statistics provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding non-Hermitian quantum dynamics, which is crucial for open quantum systems.
